thread:
maya: Pager: embeddings-v2 in us-west1 showing high error rate :rotating_light: — spike started ~06:12 UTC, roughly 30% request errors on /v1/embeddings. customers A & B reported timeouts.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260314-embeddings-high-error (severity: P1). Pager sent to oncall.
chris: I'm on the pager, doing quick triage. seeing a lot of `inconsistent shard assignment` errors from router logs.
chris: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-14T06:14:03Z ERROR rpc: inconsistent shard assignment: expected 3, got 2
2026-03-14T06:14:07Z ERROR kvcache: attempt to read missing shard 3
```
sam: that looks like a placement/placement-cache mismatch — suspect autoscaler added nodes and some routers didn't refresh placement map fast enough.
lee: can we reroute traffic to a stable fallback model (embeddings-quantized-v1) while we investigate? accuracy tradeoff but stable.
chris: will prepare a reroute + shrink of the new pool. plan: 1) set route to fallback 2) scale down canary/new pool 3) force placement refresh. Commands I plan to run:
```
rdwctl route set --service embeddings --to embeddings-quantized-v1 --weight 100 --reason "mitigate shard mismatch"
rdwctl pool resize --name embeddings-usw1-canary --replicas 0 --grace 60
rdwctl placement refresh --force --service embeddings
```
maya: running the first two commands now, pinging metrics.
sam: watching metrics — error rate is dropping from ~30% -> 3% within a minute :thumbsup:. latency stable.
nana (customer-success): notified customers A and B, they're ok with temporary fallback for now. will keep them posted.
alex (product): please capture the customer impact details in the postmortem; we need to know if this should change Q2 roadmap priorities.
chris: early root cause hypothesis: placement refresh race condition under rapid autoscaler events. capturing traces and rpc logs to confirm.
maya: handing off incident lead to chris at 06:45 UTC for post-incident follow-ups.
chris: proposing postmortem meeting 2026-03-15 17:00 UTC (invite to eng-sre, eng-runtime, product, support) — will share notes beforehand.
lee: suggested action items (quick draft):
- A1: Fix placement refresh race (owner: chris, size: L, accept criteria: no stale placement seen after autoscaler events)
- A2: Add cross-zone canary + health-checks before routing 100% (owner: sam, size: M, accept criteria: canary passes cross-zone checks for 10 mins)
- A3: Improve fallback/runbook & SLO comms (owner: alex, size: S, accept criteria: runbook published + templates)
- A4: Customer outreach template for degraded fallback (owner: ana, size: S, accept criteria: template approved by support)
chris: I'll add A1 to runtime backlog and link the logs/traces. estimate ~5d for A1.
sam: A2 depends on autoscaler hooks, estimate 3 engineer-days => size M.
alex: for Q2 planning, recommend A1/A2 be prioritized in sprint 2; A3/A4 can be sprint 3. tie them to reliability OKR.
maya: creating tickets now and assigning owners, will include acceptance criteria and links to traces. tickets: 
- RDW-1209 Fix placement refresh race (owner: chris, estimate: 5d, label: incident-fix)
- RDW-1210 Canary cross-zone checks (owner: sam, estimate: 3d, label: reliability)
- RDW-1211 Fallback runbook & SLO notes (owner: alex, estimate: 1d, label: docs)
- RDW-1212 Customer outreach template (owner: ana, estimate: 1d, label: comms)
lee: recommend a short blameless writeup summarizing timeline and impact in #incidents for org visibility.
chris: will draft the postmortem one-pager and post to #incidents for review, linking RDW-1209 and RDW-1210.
maya: summary: mitigated by reroute to fallback, scaling down canary and forcing placement refresh. errors returned to baseline, impact limited to two customers on canary. postmortem scheduled, 4 action items created and sized with Q2 tie-ins.
maya: handing off oncall and marking incident mitigated.
incident-bot: Incident INC-20260314-embeddings-high-error marked resolved by maya at 06:52 UTC.
sam: nice work all — please update tickets with PR links and timestamped test evidence. follow-ups due EOD Friday.
nana (customer-success): I'll follow up with account leads and confirm customers are satisfied with remediation.
chris: thanks everyone — I'll post the draft postmortem in #incidents and ping reviewers once ready.
maya: end of thread — thanks team :heart:
